03 · Two the drawing found

Neither is in the original 18. Both are contradictions that only appear once real numbers are on a real screen.
N1 · NEW · SHEET 04 · NEEDS A RULING

The cap chip and the cap gauge can disagree

The Garage chip shows the bare cap; the car page's gauge shows the pooled budget. §5.3 makes that difference deliberate — but it does not say what happens at the boundary.

at 1.600 km driven:
chip  1.600/1.500 → "100 km over"
gauge 1.600/1.760 → "under the cap"

Two surfaces, one car, opposite verdicts — which §C4 forbids outright.

WHAT I DREW, PENDING YOUR CALL

The chip keeps showing the bare cap as its numbers, but its over/under state follows the pooled budget — and when it flips it names the pooled overage. So the two can differ in figure, never in verdict.

#16 · FROM THE ORIGINAL 18 · STILL UNDRAWN

A flagged reading inside an Insights page

A reading the user has not accepted still feeds the bars. So a period can render as a clean, confident chart built partly on data that is under dispute — and nothing on the page says so.

This is the honesty rules turned on Insights itself. Article 4 says show the math; a disputed input is part of the math.

THE WIREFRAMES' RECOMMENDATION, WHICH I ENDORSE
Some readings in this period need a decision. Review notes ›

One quiet ink line under the headline. Not attention, not a badge on the bars, not a suppressed chart — the numbers are still the best available, and the line is a receipt, not a warning.
